takeaways: In the AM window (09:30–11:00 ET), Wednesday has historically been the strongest weekday (+0.023% avg, 53% win rate, n=987) and Friday the weakest (-0.029%, 50% win rate, n=965).

By month, February AM sessions have run hottest (+0.056% avg, n=384) and September the coldest (-0.043%, n=407) — a single month is a thin sample (~384 days across 19 years), so treat this as a mild tilt, not a rule.
Turn-of-month days (first 3 / last 2 trading days) show an edge over mid-month: +0.020% vs +0.004% AM average (54% vs 52% win rate).
Around holidays: the day before averages +0.011% AM and the day after +0.071%, both on small samples (n=176/176) vs +0.005% on a normal day — directional, not something to size a trade around.

Context on all of the above: the typical single day's AM move spans roughly 1.48 percentage points (10th-to-90th percentile) — about 29x the 0.052-point gap between the best and worst weekday average. Day-to-day noise dwarfs the seasonal tilt; these are mild, long-run leans, not a signal for any one day.
